acceptance_criteria.criterion: A sequence diagram / executable contract documents exactly which boundary owns: focused dev verification, pre-push safety, hosted full exact-head proof, candidate admission, PR integration compatibility, and merge readiness.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/VALIDATION_STAGE_CONTRACT.md carries the mermaid sequence diagram and the ownership table; docs/VALIDATION_STAGE_CONTRACT.json is the machine-readable form declaring owner, boundary, proof, full_repository_suite policy and a must_not per stage. tests/test_validation_stage_contract.py::test_contract_declares_the_whole_pipeline_in_order pins all seven stages in pipeline order, and ::test_documented_contract_covers_every_declared_stage binds the prose to the manifest.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No normal candidate can execute the same full repository Pytest suite more than once for the same immutable candidate identity unless the validation definition/configuration changed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Any proof reuse is keyed to immutable content identity plus a deterministic validation-definition identity; stale/mismatched receipts are refused.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Benchmark evidence is recorded from before and after on representative repository state. Target: final code change -> reviewable PR normally <= 5–8 minutes hosted wall-clock, or document the measured limiting factor if infrastructure prevents that target.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Hunter / Pre-PR Preflight on this same branch: 10m00s at base afcee3c, 5m13s at 25b0745. Hosted Pytest 536.55s/3628 to 250.80s/3710. acceptance_criteria.criterion: No accepted ADR is modified unless independent architecture review proves a binding architectural conflict. Prefer an implementation/governance optimization under existing authority.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: No file under docs/ADR/ is in the reviewed change set. The contribution introduces no new authority or registry: the stage contract documents ownership that already existed, and the reuse authority is a derived, non-durable identity check. The only policy edit adds two root_of_trust_paths entries, which narrows the connector grant rather than widening it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No merge, auto-merge, or force-push from this contribution.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: PR #416 is Draft and unmerged; auto-merge was never enabled. Every push to origin/issue-415-validation-performance has been fast-forward (afcee3c..327242b..25b0745..46e3ecd..d778351). One amend occurred before the branch was ever pushed, so no published history was rewritten.

defect_families.evidence: The candidate mints one new proof object, and it cannot be replayed: a receipt binds the exact Git tree, the definition identity and the toolchain, and verify() refuses on any mismatch before any acceptance branch is reached. There is no path in verify() that accepts a receipt on the strength of something the receipt itself asserts. The head binding additionally stops two heads carrying an identical tree from borrowing each other's proof (::test_foreign_head_proof_fails_closed). The connector authorization receipt is untouched by this candidate.

A hand-edited receipt is detectable because none of its identities are trusted: each is recomputed by the verifier from content it already holds, so an edited receipt can only narrow reuse, never widen it. The CI resolver never reads a candidate-supplied artifact at all -- its anchors are Git content addressing and the Actions run record, neither of which a writer can forge. Receipts are git-ignored, so no forged receipt can travel in a candidate.

No channel's proof obligation changed. The trusted hosted exact-head proof stays required for every candidate, which is why no PREFLIGHT_OWNED_PATHS entry was added for the new files: require_for_all_candidates already covers them. tests/test_validation_proof_reuse.py::test_reuse_names_the_same_trusted_workflow_candidate_admission_requires pins the reuse resolver's workflow name and path to the trusted controller's constants so the two cannot drift into meaning different proofs.

Every commit in afcee3c..d778351 carries author and committer Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>, the identity bound to login 'claude' in writer_identity_binding; agent attribution is carried in Co-Authored-By and Claude-Session trailers only. _validate_writer_provenance still runs at the push boundary before any network mutation and was exercised on each of the four pushes.

The range is four commits, each pushed as it was made, and each is a substantive content change: no intermediate commit is stranded and no rewind or force-push was needed at any point. The one amend happened before the branch existed on the remote.

_validate_receipt_freshness is unchanged and still runs before the lane. This candidate writes no connector authorization receipt, so the inherited-receipt path applies and correctly makes no claim about this range. The separately introduced validation receipt is deliberately not a published artifact: it is git-ignored, so it can never be the stale receipt this family is about, and recording it is best-effort so a cache failure cannot turn a green run red.

verify_pre_ready_hostile_review is unmodified and still gates admission. This review is the artifact that family requires: recorded against the exact base->HEAD content, covering all eleven applicable families and all twelve Issue #415 acceptance criteria, with no unresolved blocking finding. Its correct operation was observed live -- it blocked this very candidate while the inherited Issue #390 review was on the branch.

No prerequisite reporting path was changed. The new CI resolver never publishes a status; it emits a step output and always exits 0, so an unavailable prerequisite makes CI run the full lane rather than publish a spurious failure. Observed live on this PR: Hunter Governance Review reported the absent trusted proof while it was still running, then advanced to the next gate once it landed.

Two families are added and neither overclaims. DFF-016 claims hosted-enforced and carries a resolvable non-test guard reference (hunter_validation_receipt.py::verify) at a machine boundary plus six resolvable regression tests. DFF-017 claims only regression-tested with a review boundary and no guard_reference, which is the honest stage for an invariant whose enforcement is a pytest fixture rather than a gate symbol. PRH-007's explicit_enforcement local field was rewritten to describe what the boundary now actually does rather than leaving a stale claim standing.

This is the family the candidate introduces, and independent owner review found its invariant was not actually enforced on one of the two production paths: the local reuse caller omitted the head binding while the push boundary supplied it, so content identity alone decided reuse there. Repaired by making the binding non-optional rather than by remembering to pass it -- verify() has no default for head_sha, and reuse_blocker resolves it from the repository when a caller has not. Adversarially probed beyond that: a run of another workflow wearing the same name, a non-push event, a superseded green run for the same head, a foreign-head run, a malformed payload and unavailable git evidence are each refused by their own fixture, and the same-tree different-commit case is now driven through the production caller rather than the verifier.

This family exists because the candidate committed the defect and it was caught by the trusted controller on head 327242b. Repaired in 25b0745 by moving the worker flags to the hosted steps that install the plugin, then made enforceable in d778351 by four fixtures covering placement, provisioning, distribution-only semantics and loud failure when the plugin is absent. Each fixture was verified against its own injected violation and only its own.

findings.evidence: Pinning -n auto --dist loadfile in the candidate's own [tool.pytest.ini_options] made the candidate's own trusted validation unrunnable: Trusted Candidate Preflight Validation on head 327242b failed with 'pytest: error: unrecognized arguments: -n --dist loadfile' because the trusted controller executes this repository's gate commands inside the candidate tree under the trusted environment, which has no reason to carry the plugin. Repaired in 25b0745 by moving the lane to PYTEST_ADDOPTS on the two hosted steps that install the pinned dev extra; verified against a clean interpreter carrying only the trusted pins, which collects all 3710 tests with no xdist installed. Registered as DFF-017. Trusted Candidate Preflight Validation has concluded success on every head since.

DFF-017's first applicability scope listed 'requirements/', which silently widened the pre-ready hostile-review applicable-family set onto the dependency manifests that tests/test_issue_412_prevention_gate.py::test_dependency_manifests_are_deliberately_outside_the_review_scope pins as deliberately out of scope. That pinned fixture caught it. Repaired by narrowing the scope to pyproject.toml and scripts/hunter_pr_preflight.py: adding a pin is not the defect, requiring it from a configuration the trusted environment must execute under is.

CI proof reuse is opportunistic rather than deterministic: a branch push and its pull-request event fire seconds apart, so Quality Gates usually starts before the proof it could reuse exists and correctly refuses. Recorded in docs/VALIDATION_STAGE_CONTRACT.md rather than fixed, because the two hosted lanes run concurrently and making CI wait for a reusable proof would raise wall-clock time in order to lower it. Reuse still fires on re-runs and whenever the proof lands first, and the invariant it enforces -- identical content is never validated twice -- holds regardless.

report_full_repository_proof_ownership catches broadly and degrades to a NOTE. Deliberate and asserted by review of the call site: the function is informational only, so a failure to report which boundary owns the full proof must never block a push that has already satisfied every enforcing check. It cannot mask an enforcement failure because it runs after the lane and owns no verdict.

Independent owner review of head fda1ad0 found that the local validation-receipt reuse path did not bind reuse to the current HEAD: hunter_pr_preflight._reuse_blocker() called receipts.reuse_blocker(root) without a head, reuse_blocker defaulted head_sha to None, and verify() skipped the head comparison, so a receipt recorded for commit A could authorize a different commit B carrying the same tree, definition and toolchain. The finding is correct and the strongest evidence for it was internal: the push boundary passed the head while the preflight caller did not, and this review's own DFF-016 answer had asserted the binding held. Repaired by removing the default -- verify() now requires head_sha, so the binding cannot be dropped by omitting a keyword, and reuse_blocker resolves the head itself when a caller has not established one. The regression drives the production caller with two real commits resolving to the same tree (an amended message), and was confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the repair; a second fixture pins that verify() cannot be called without the binding at all. Recorded as RFD-416-001 and folded into DFF-016's prevention mechanism.
